title: By the night, when it covers everything.
subtitle: The first of three pairs of opposites
then: Ibn Kathir says the night here {idea}covers the creation with its darkness{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ named this surah, with Ash-Shams, as one to recite in the night prayer. {idea}Its oaths are opposites, because its subject is opposite ways of living.{/idea}
now: You are on the night bus home and the whole city has gone dark except the shop signs. Everyone around you lived a different day. {idea}Same night, very different efforts.{/idea} That is where this surah is heading.
old: Night is just the time between one day and the next.
new: The night is sworn by to set up a contrast I need to see in my own life.
try: Tonight, before sleep, recall one thing you did today and ask which way it pointed.

title: And by the day, when it shines out.
subtitle: Light set against the covering dark
then: The day comes {reward}with its light and its radiance{/reward}, Ibn Kathir says. Placed right after the night, it makes the contrast obvious. The surah introduction says human efforts differ {idea}as much as day differs from night{/idea}.
now: People say everyone is just doing their best and it all comes out the same. But you know a colleague who covers for others and one who takes credit. {idea}They are not the same, any more than noon is midnight.{/idea}
old: In the end, everyone's choices kind of balance out.
new: Good and bad efforts are as different as day and night.
try: Notice one bright act someone did for you today and thank them for it.

title: By the One who created male and female.
subtitle: Creation made in pairs
then: Ibn Kathir links this to {idea}We created you in pairs{/idea} and {idea}of everything We created pairs{/idea}. Just as the things sworn by are opposites, he says, so is what the oath is about.
now: Think of your parents, or a couple you know well. Different in so many ways, made to complement. {idea}Pairs are everywhere in creation.{/idea} Your choices come in pairs too: give or keep, tell the truth or hide it.
old: These oaths are just poetic openings.
new: Creation in pairs prepares me to see my own choices as pairs.
try: Name one decision today where you can see the two sides clearly, and pick the better one.

title: Your efforts are not all the same.
subtitle: The point all three oaths were leading to
then: This is the answer to the oaths. Ibn Kathir: {idea}the actions of the servants are also opposites and diverse{/idea}. There are those who do good and those who do evil. Early Makkans were all busy, but not all heading the same way.
now: Your calendar is packed. Meetings, school runs, side projects, the gym. {trap}Being busy feels like being good.{/trap} {idea}The verse asks what all that running is for.{/idea}
old: As long as I am working hard, I am doing well.
new: What matters is the direction of my effort, not how much of it there is.
try: Look at tomorrow's plans and mark one item that is truly for Allah's sake.

title: The first path starts with giving and being mindful.
subtitle: Two traits of the easy road
then: Ibn Kathir explains: {reward}he gives what he has been commanded to give{/reward} and {idea}fears Allah in his affairs{/idea}. The surah introduction counts these as the first marks of one way of life.
now: Payday comes. Before the rent and the takeaway, you set aside a little for someone who needs it. You also stop yourself cutting a corner on your expense claim. {reward}Giving and being careful, side by side.{/reward}
old: Giving is for people who have spare money.
new: Giving and watching myself before Allah are where the good path begins.
try: Give something small today, even a few coins, without telling anyone.

title: He believes the best reward is real.
subtitle: Giving because you trust what comes back
then: Qatadah said the best here means {reward}the compensation{/reward} for what he gives. Khusayf said it means the reward. {idea}His giving rests on believing that it is not lost.{/idea}
now: You hover over the donate button and a voice says you might need this money next month. The person who presses it anyway is not careless. {reward}They believe the return is real.{/reward}
old: Whatever I give away is just gone.
new: What I give is stored with Allah, who repays with the best.
try: Before you give anything today, say quietly that you trust its reward.

title: Allah makes the good road easy for him.
subtitle: Each good step makes the next one lighter

row.title: it is written, so why act?
act, it is made easy
sub: for what you were made for

then: Ibn Abbas said the ease here means {reward}goodness{/reward}. Companions asked the Prophet ﷺ why act if all is decreed. He said: {idea}Perform deeds, for everyone will have made easy what he was created for{/idea}, then recited these verses.
now: The first week of waking for Fajr is brutal. By the third week your body wakes itself. {reward}That is the ease the verse promises{/reward}: you take a step, and Allah smooths the road ahead.
old: Doing good will always feel this hard.
new: When I keep stepping toward good, Allah makes the road smoother.
try: Pick one good habit that feels heavy and do it once today, trusting it gets lighter.

title: The other path: holding back, and needing no one.
subtitle: Stinginess paired with self-sufficiency

row.title: I earned it, it is mine
I need Allah
sub: and what I have is His

then: Ibn Abbas said this means {trap}he is stingy with his wealth and considers himself in no need of his Lord{/trap}. The two go together. The surah introduction lists them as the opposite marks of the first person.
now: Your savings are healthy, your job is secure, and prayer has quietly slipped. {trap}You did not decide to stop needing Allah. You just started feeling fine without Him.{/trap} Comfort can do that.
old: I have what I need, I can manage on my own.
new: Feeling self-sufficient is the start of the hard road, however comfortable it feels.
try: Make one short dua today asking for something you think you already have.

title: He calls the promised reward a lie.
subtitle: Denying that the Hereafter repays anything
then: Ibn Kathir says the best here is {reward}the recompense in the abode of the Hereafter{/reward}. This man denies it. {trap}If nothing comes back, holding on to everything makes sense to him.{/trap}
now: A friend says charity is a nice idea but you have to look after number one. It sounds practical. {trap}Underneath it is a bet that nothing given is ever repaid.{/trap}
old: Only what I keep is really mine.
new: If I doubt the reward, I will always find reasons not to give.
try: Think about one thing you gave that came back to you in some way. Thank Allah for it.

title: For him, the hard road gets easier to walk.
subtitle: Wrong becomes easy, good becomes hard
then: Ibn Kathir says this is {trap}the path of evil{/trap}, and cites: {trap}We shall leave them in their trespass to wander blindly{/trap}. Whoever intends good is helped to success; whoever intends evil is left to it.
now: The first time you lied to get out of something, your heart raced. Now it is automatic. {trap}The wrong road has become smooth.{/trap} {idea}That ease is a warning, not a comfort.{/idea}
old: If it feels easy, it must be fine.
new: When wrong starts feeling easy, that is the hard road being smoothed for me.
try: Name one wrong thing that has become easy for you. Make it a little harder to do today.

title: His money will not catch him when he falls.
subtitle: What wealth cannot do at the end
then: This closes the first half of the surah. The man {trap}kept his wealth and felt no need of his Lord{/trap}. Now the question: what will that wealth do for him when he goes down? {idea}The answer is nothing.{/idea}
now: You sit in a hospital corridor waiting for news. Your bank balance is the same as yesterday, and it means nothing right now. {idea}What you need in that moment, money cannot buy.{/idea}
old: As long as I have money, I am covered.
new: Wealth I held back will not hold me up when I fall.
try: Use some of what you have today to help someone, so it becomes something that lasts.
